title: AI Guidelines for Business Ver 1.0 (Provisional Translation)

policy_extraction.issuing_body: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) and Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
covered_actors: AI business actors involved in advanced AI systems
Public institutions (such as governments and municipalities) acting as AI business actors
prohibited_practices: Developing, providing, or using AI systems and services with the purpose of manipulating human decision-making, recognition, and emotion or on the premise of unconscious control
Using AI for profiling in fields where personal rights and benefits can be severely affected for inappropriate purposes

evidence.quote: Conduct appropriate risk analyses to take countermeasures against risks (avoidance, mitigation, transference, or acceptance).

evidence.quote: Each AI business actor first conducts an environment and risk analysis for the AI system or service based on the benefits and risks the AI system or service may bring about during the overall lifecycle, social acceptance relating to the development and operation, changes in the external environment, and the maturity of AI.
evidence.source_section: Part 2, E. Building AI governance

evidence.quote: Take appropriate measures throughout the development of advanced AI systems, including prior to and throughout their deployment and placement on the market, to identify, evaluate, and mitigate risks across the AI lifecycle.

evidence.quote: Ensure controllability that allows humans to control AI as necessary including objective monitoring and handling, in accordance with the characteristics and purposes of the relevant AI, in light of the severity and possibility of rights violations that can result from AI use or unintended AI behaviors.

evidence.quote: To prevent AI from generating unfair results, consider implementing timely human interventions, rather than letting AI make the decisions alone.
evidence.source_section: Part 2, C. Common Guiding Principles, 3) Fairness

evidence.quote: In accordance with the characteristics and purposes of AI systems and services, ensure the accuracy, and recency as necessary, of the data (appropriateness of the data) to be used for training.

evidence.quote: Properly collect training data through privacy-by-design, etc., and if it contains third-parties' personal data, data requiring attention to intellectual property rights, etc., ensure that such data is properly handled in compliance with laws and regulations throughout the lifecycle of AI ("2) Safety," "4) Privacy protection," "5) Ensuring security").

evidence.quote: If any open technologies are used, conform to the rules specified for them. • When disclose developed AI systems as open source, consider any potential social impacts.

policy_extraction.implementation_notes: Jointly issued by MIC and METI on April 19, 2024 (provisional English translation), integrating and revising three earlier Japanese guidelines (AI R&D Guidelines, AI Utilization Guidelines, and Governance Guidelines for Implementation of AI Principles ver. 1.1). Explicitly framed as non-binding soft law promoting voluntary, risk-based, and agile governance, maintained as a living document. Incorporates the G7 Hiroshima AI Process International Guiding Principles and Code of Conduct for advanced AI systems (including foundation models and generative AI). Explicitly excludes non-business users and data providers from its direct scope while advising compliance with existing applicable laws (e.g., Act on the Protection of Personal Information and intellectual property laws).

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The document's dominant framing is innovation_enablement because its core justification for adopting voluntary, goal-based, risk-based, and agile soft-law guidelines is to avoid stifling AI innovation while mitigating risks that could cause social disagreement and inhibit AI adoption. Fundamental_rights is a close runner-up, anchoring Part 2's normative philosophies in human dignity, constitutional and international human rights, fairness, privacy, and democracy; however, innovation_enablement edges it out as the overarching rationale explaining why MIC and METI chose flexible business guidelines over binding rules to realize Society 5.0. Secondary rationales include consumer_public_safety (preventing harm to lives, bodies, minds, and property), economic_competitiveness (strengthening competitiveness and sustainable economic growth), social_stability (countering society-destabilizing disinformation and avoiding social divisions), and labor_transition (addressing labor shortages and promoting education and reskilling as human-AI task division shifts).

evidence_spans.quote: Thus, it was decided to draw up guidelines on the basis of the goal-based concept that would lead to the achievement of purposes through soft laws without any legally binding force that would encourage interested parties to make voluntary efforts to reduce societal risks in AI and promote innovations and use of AI.

When developing, providing, or using an AI system or service, each AI business actor should act in a way that does not violate the human rights guaranteed by the Constitution of Japan or granted internationally, as the foundation for accomplishing all matters to be conducted, including the matters described later.
evidence_spans.source_section: Part 2, C. Common Guiding Principles, 1) Human-Centric

evidence_spans.quote: Each AI business actor should avoid damage to the lives, bodies, minds, and properties of stakeholders during the development, provision, and use of AI systems and services. In addition, it is important that the environment is not damaged.
evidence_spans.source_section: Part 2, C. Common Guiding Principles, 2) Safety

evidence_spans.quote: Paying close attention to these possibilities enables to maximize the benefits from AI, strengthen competitiveness, and maintain and improve the business values.

Generative AI has enabled everyone to forge fake information that seems to be true and fair, so recognize the increasing risk of destabilizing and confusing the society through disinformation, misinformation, and biased information generated by AI, and take necessary countermeasures
evidence_spans.source_section: Part 2, C. Common Guiding Principles, 1) Human-Centric (3)

evidence_spans.quote: It is assumed that the division of tasks between AI and humans will change due to the expansion of generative AI use, so discuss actively about education and reskilling to promote new ways of working.
evidence_spans.source_section: Part 2, C. Common Guiding Principles, 8) Education/literacy (2)
